basis: Independent review of the original treatment brief and exact revealed plan; source identities and IDs retained from the investigator map, with critic primary-source checks added below.

sources.title: Rain gardens (bioretention) 101
sources.publisher: Minnesota Pollution Control Agency, Minnesota Stormwater Manual
sources.version_or_release: Living online manual; no page revision date/version displayed in accessed page (© 2026 MPCA).
sources.locator: How does a rain garden work? and What maintenance is needed; page lines 62-91.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official page and reviewed the cited sections.
sources.observed_findings: Distinguishes underdrained from non-underdrained rain gardens; describes street-curb-cut routing, ponding and drainage, low-infiltration soils, monthly inlet inspection, debris/soil removal, and avoiding trampling/compaction.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: General educational description; drainage route depends on whether an underdrain is present. The one-to-two-day drainage statement is guidance, not an identified site or local permit condition.
sources.applicability: Mechanism and inspection baseline. Does not identify this hypothetical garden's layers, drawdown criterion, site performance, or governing jurisdiction.

critic_review.observed_operation: Opened the official MPCA page and reviewed its rain-garden mechanism, underdrain, drainage-time, and maintenance text.
critic_review.observed_findings: Confirms the underdrain/no-underdrain distinction, curb-cut routing, ponding then percolation or underdrain flow, a general one-to-two-day drainage statement, and routine inlet inspections.
critic_review.governing_condition_default_exception: Educational Minnesota manual guidance; its drainage statement is not a local requirement for this hypothetical site.
critic_review.applicability: Supports the draft's process distinctions and maintenance inquiry only; does not establish this garden's configuration or criterion.

sources.title: Overview for bioretention
sources.publisher: Minnesota Pollution Control Agency, Minnesota Stormwater Manual
sources.version_or_release: Living online manual; no page revision date/version displayed.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official page and reviewed the high-flow bypass section.
sources.observed_findings: Describes offline and online bypass, curb-cut bypass after maximum ponding, the possibility of gutter bypass by design, erosion risk, and the risk of short-circuiting.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: High-flow bypass is expected when inflow exceeds the design water-quality volume or cell capacity; online routes need erosion/short-circuit care.
sources.applicability: Supports treating bypass as an observation to interpret against as-builts and event context, not automatically a malfunction. Minnesota design recommendations may not govern the unspecified site.

critic_review.observed_operation: Opened the official MPCA bioretention overview and reviewed the water-quantity/bypass section.
critic_review.observed_findings: Confirms high-flow bypass when cells fill, offline gutter bypass after maximum ponding, and erosion/short-circuiting considerations.
critic_review.governing_condition_default_exception: The described bypass is tied to design volume/cell capacity and flow-path configuration; the page is Minnesota guidance, not evidence of this site's intent.
critic_review.applicability: Supports interpreting observed pass-by against as-builts and event size rather than labeling it a defect.

sources.title: Green Streets Handbook
sources.locator: Chapter 4, sections 4.4-4.5; PDF pp. 45-53, including curb cuts, pretreatment, bypass and underdrains.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official PDF and reviewed relevant text.
sources.observed_findings: Curb-cut placement in gutter flow path, grading toward practice, high-flow gutter bypass, low-profile berm/runnel as a site-dependent alternative, grates/trench drains, pretreatment for sediment/debris, bypass/overflow and underdrain tradeoffs.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Curb opening behavior depends on placement, slope, flow rate and practice capacity. Underdrains are a conditional management approach; local dewatering rules differ.
sources.applicability: Alternatives and mechanisms for a qualified partner to compare. Contains design examples and dimensions that are not adopted as prescriptions here.

critic_review.observed_operation: Opened the official EPA February 2021 PDF and reviewed Chapter 4 curb-cut placement, grading, and bypass text.
critic_review.locator: PDF pp. 45-53; parsed text around lines 1792-1827 and 2034-2055.
critic_review.observed_findings: Confirms flow-path placement, grading toward the practice, bypass at capacity, and a site-dependent berm/runnel option for steep gutter lines.
critic_review.governing_condition_default_exception: These are design considerations conditioned on local flow and geometry; the handbook is guidance and gives dimensions that are not adopted in the proposal.
critic_review.applicability: Supports conditional alternatives for partner review, not a retrofit recommendation or local design.

sources.title: Operation and maintenance of bioretention and other stormwater infiltration practices
sources.publisher: Minnesota Pollution Control Agency, Minnesota Stormwater Manual
sources.version_or_release: Living online manual; no page revision date/version displayed.
sources.locator: Post-Construction Phase O&M and common problems; lines 156-210.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official page and reviewed inspection schedule, maintenance cautions and symptom table.
sources.observed_findings: Recommends post-storm and routine checks of ponding, inlets/outlets/bypass, debris, sediment, vegetation and erosion; cautions against traffic/foot traffic compaction; lists leaves, sediment and plant debris as possible flow-path obstructions and surface sediment/loading as possible slow-drawdown causes.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Schedule varies by year of operation, season and site. First-year checks follow storms over 0.5 inches; later checks include semiannual 48-hour post-event checks when ground is not frozen; deep sumps may hold water.
sources.applicability: Useful condition checklist, not a mandatory standard for this unnamed site. The 48-hour observation is not asserted as a local compliance requirement.

critic_review.observed_operation: Opened the official MPCA O&M page and checked its inspection table and common-problems table.
critic_review.observed_findings: Confirms first-year post-storm inspection entries, later semiannual checks at 48 hours after rain when ground is not frozen (with deep-sump caveat), debris-related flow obstruction, and standing water beyond 48 hours as a symptom associated with possible sediment/clogging.
critic_review.governing_condition_default_exception: Guidance schedule varies by operation stage and season; 48 hours is not a universal regulatory threshold and deep sumps can retain water.
critic_review.applicability: Supports conditional observation and maintenance review only; the draft states the locality caveat correctly.

sources.title: Operation and Maintenance of Green Infrastructure Receiving Runoff from Roads and Parking Lots: Technical Memorandum
sources.version_or_release: 2016 technical memorandum; PDF is the EPA-hosted published edition.
sources.locator: Inspection and Assessment; pp. 7-12, especially lines 272-322 and 364-378; pretreatment discussion pp. 6-7.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official PDF and reviewed inspection, drawdown and assessment sections.
sources.observed_findings: Inspection cadence depends on drainage area, land use, watershed activities and rain magnitude/intensity; staff gauges or repeated levels can track drawdown; records to gather include design specifications and past maintenance; standing water at 48 hours can trigger further investigation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The memo frames 48 hours as an example investigation trigger and calls for site-specific criteria/qualified assessment; it is not a universal rule.
sources.applicability: Supports the records-first and low-impact observation proposal; does not diagnose this site's infiltration or establish local thresholds.

critic_review.observed_operation: Opened the official EPA 2016 memorandum and checked inspection triggers, measurement approaches, and the records/assessment discussion.
critic_review.locator: PDF pp. 7-10; parsed text lines 272-300 and 368-378.
critic_review.observed_findings: Confirms that standing water at 48 hours is an example trigger for further evaluation; inspection frequency varies with drainage area, watershed activity, and rainfall; a staff gage or other level measure can track decline; design specifications and past maintenance are inputs to assessment.
critic_review.governing_condition_default_exception: The 48-hour language is an example for qualified further evaluation, not a site-specific or universal compliance standard.
critic_review.applicability: Supports the records-first and safe drawdown-observation proposal, not a diagnosis or required local threshold.

sources.title: Assessing the performance of stormwater Best Management Practices (BMPs)
sources.publisher: Minnesota Pollution Control Agency, Minnesota Stormwater Manual
sources.version_or_release: Living online manual; page notes underlying assessment manual was developed in 2010; no current page revision date displayed.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official page and reviewed assessment level descriptions and effort/limitations.
sources.observed_findings: Visual inspection is quick/inexpensive but limited; capacity, simulated runoff and long-term monitoring add effort and answer different questions. Visual results do not establish numeric credits.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Owners seeking regulatory credit from testing must consult the responsible agency; effort/time table is a general planning aid.
sources.applicability: Supports phased observation then justified escalation. No assessment or performance test was executed.

critic_review.observed_operation: Opened the official MPCA BMP-assessment page and reviewed its four-level summary.
critic_review.observed_findings: Confirms visual inspection, capacity tests, synthetic-runoff tests, and monitoring as distinct assessment levels; Level 1 does not yield numeric performance data.
critic_review.governing_condition_default_exception: Level choice depends on objective and effort; credit use requires agency consultation.
critic_review.applicability: Supports a staged observation then escalation plan and the draft's distinction between visual evidence and performance claims.

sources.title: Overview and methods of pretreatment
sources.publisher: Minnesota Pollution Control Agency, Minnesota Stormwater Manual
sources.version_or_release: Living online manual; no page revision date/version displayed.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official page and reviewed pretreatment selection conditions.
sources.observed_findings: Selection depends on debris/pollutant, space, topography and receiving flow; filter strips are associated with sheet flow and small gardens, forebays with channelized flow, and screens with leaves/large debris.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Examples assume no overriding site limitations; no device is universally preferred.
sources.applicability: Frames alternatives for the city partner after flow type and access are known; it does not authorize or size a retrofit.

critic_review.observed_operation: Opened the official MPCA pretreatment page and reviewed its applicability section.
critic_review.observed_findings: Confirms selection by site conditions and receiving flow; filter strips are indicated for sheet flow/small residential rain gardens, above-ground forebays for channelized flow, and screens for leaves/large debris.
critic_review.governing_condition_default_exception: Examples assume no overriding limitations; pretreatment is not a stand-alone treatment and must match the downstream practice and maintenance capacity.
critic_review.applicability: Supports the draft's conditional alternatives, not a device selection for this site.

sources.title: Capture of gross solids and sediment by pretreatment practices for bioretention
sources.publisher: University of Minnesota Water Resources Center / St. Anthony Falls Laboratory project
sources.version_or_release: Final report by A. Erickson and M. Hernick, SAFL Project Report No. 586, January 2019; 2022 research brief also listed by the official project page.
sources.locator: Project overview, tested practices and findings; lines 13-38; report links at lines 43-46.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official UMN project page at the recorded access time and reviewed its project summary and listed report metadata. The full report text was not reviewed.
sources.observed_findings: Field tests compared grass-lined and rock-lined inlets, Rain Guardian Bunker/Turret and shallow sump. Reported capture varied between low/high intensity; overflow in tested sump reduced gross-solid capture; summary reports Bunker/Turret easier to maintain than grass/rock inlet.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Test method/intensity and device configurations bound results; this is pretreatment capture evidence, not full-garden field performance or product endorsement.
sources.applicability: Offers unfamiliar alternatives and maintenance tradeoffs for partner discussion; no result is transferred as expected local efficiency.

critic_review.observed_operation: Opened the official University of Minnesota Water Resources Center project summary and reviewed tested configurations and findings; the full linked report was not downloaded or inspected.
critic_review.locator: Official project page lines 15-32 and report links at 43-46.
critic_review.observed_findings: Confirms five tested configurations; low/high-intensity results; reduced gross-solids capture in the tested shallow sump under overflow; and relative maintenance findings for Bunker/Turret versus grass/rock inlets.
critic_review.governing_condition_default_exception: Findings are bounded to the study's devices and test method; they do not establish whole-garden performance or product suitability here.
critic_review.applicability: The draft uses the results only as bounded comparison evidence, which is appropriate.

sources.title: Designing Holistic Bioretention for Performance and Longevity (Bioretention Design Handbook)
sources.locator: Chapter 14, section 14.2, Inlets and Inspection and Maintenance Activities; PDF/text pages 14-4 and following, lines 8094-8128.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the EPA-hosted text edition and reviewed inlet maintenance guidance.
sources.observed_findings: Calls for clearing inlets/pretreatment to prevent occlusion, bypass, clogging and channelization; advises inspection during/after storms for grading or inlet damage and debris/sediment buildup.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The handbook itself states it is guidance and that site design must follow local conditions/rules; its example maintenance frequencies are not local requirements.
sources.applicability: Supports storm-time/after-event visual observations and event/history records. No proposed repair or design dimension is adopted.

critic_review.observed_operation: Opened the official EPA handbook text and checked Chapter 14.2 inlet and maintenance passages.
critic_review.observed_findings: Confirms checking for grading changes, inlet damage, erosion/sediment, leaves and debris that could block inflow, and clearing obstructions.
critic_review.governing_condition_default_exception: The handbook is guidance; inspection examples are not jurisdiction-specific requirements.
critic_review.applicability: Supports the draft's visual/history checklist and conditional maintenance inquiry.

sources.title: Dynamic Media Storage Links Antecedent Soil Moisture to Runoff Retention in Field-Scale Bioretention Systems
sources.version_or_release: Version of Record, published 2026-09-16; publisher notes page records original article/PDF upload on 2026-09-16.
sources.locator: Abstract and methods excerpt surfaced by publisher-indexed search result; title/abstract/methods. Publisher article URL: https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4441/18/18/2320; notes: https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4441/18/18/2320/notes.
sources.observed_operation: At the recorded access time, publisher-indexed search output exposed the abstract and methods excerpt. Full article text was not verified in this pass.
sources.observed_findings: Study reports three wet seasons of monitoring at two contrasting roof-fed Beijing facilities and event variables including rainfall depth, duration, intensity and antecedent media storage. The abstract cautions that dynamic storage depends on hydraulic loading, media configuration and drainage pathways.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Two engineered systems in Beijing differ in media, hydraulic load, lining and drainage; conclusions are case-specific and the accessible abstract is the limit of review here.
sources.applicability: Used only to justify collecting event and antecedent conditions and to caution against transfer; no reported efficiency is used as a target or prediction.

critic_review.observed_operation: Queried the DOI and official MDPI article/notes. Publisher-indexed output exposed the Version of Record metadata, abstract, and body excerpt; direct page opening through the web tool returned an internal error. The detailed five-minute rainfall method was not independently reverified beyond accessible indexed material.
critic_review.locator: Publisher article abstract and accessible methods/discussion excerpt; publisher version-notes page records the 2026-09-16 Version of Record.
critic_review.observed_findings: Confirms three wet seasons at two contrasting roof-fed Beijing systems and the paper's focus on event rainfall and antecedent media storage; it warns that interpretation depends on loading, media configuration, and drainage pathways.
critic_review.governing_condition_default_exception: Two contrasting engineered systems in Beijing; the study is case-specific and its numerical results are not transferable to this hypothetical street garden.
critic_review.applicability: Supports recording event/antecedent conditions and cautioning against transfer. The investigator source map openly limits its method claim to indexed abstract/methods material.

sources.title: Storm Water Management Model (SWMM) User's Manual, Version 5.2
sources.version_or_release: User's Manual Version 5.2, listed by EPA in February 2022.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the EPA-hosted manual and reviewed the LID representation section.
sources.observed_findings: SWMM represents LID controls with parameterized layers and a water balance; the bioretention surface can store/run on water, soil/storage layers govern movement, and optional drains/overflow may be modeled.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Model output depends on supplied geometry, rainfall, layer properties, underdrain and flow boundary inputs; it is not a direct measurement.
sources.applicability: Optional future scenario model only after verified site inputs exist. No software was installed and no model was run.

critic_review.observed_operation: Opened the official EPA SWMM 5.2 manual and reviewed the LID representation section.
critic_review.observed_findings: Confirms layer-based LID representation and a moisture balance tracking movement/storage among layers, with surface, soil, storage, overflow, and optional underdrain pathways.
critic_review.governing_condition_default_exception: Model output depends on supplied model parameters, catchment, rainfall, and drainage configuration; it is not field measurement.
critic_review.applicability: Supports only the proposed future scenario model after verified inputs; no run was performed.

sources.title: EPA SWMM repository release v5.2.4
sources.locator: Engine updates in the v5.2.4 release; release page lines 175-211.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the release history and reviewed the tagged release and fixes.
sources.observed_findings: Release records corrected LID layer water-flux calculations, invalid-input checks for LID with underdrain, gutter slope, and effective hydraulic head for curb inlets with inclined throats.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: These fixes matter to a future model using affected representations/parameters; the release page at access did not establish that v5.2.4 is the latest release in all distributions.
sources.applicability: If later modeling proceeds, confirm and pin the version used and preserve its change history; these software fixes do not establish or diagnose physical site behavior.

critic_review.observed_operation: Opened the EPA-maintained GitHub release record for v5.2.4 and reviewed the tagged commit and engine updates.
critic_review.locator: Release page lines 153-184; tag commit 7952ca8 and Build 5.2.4 (Aug 2023).
critic_review.observed_findings: Confirms corrections to LID layer water-flux rates, underdrain invalid-input checking, depressed-gutter slope calculation, and effective hydraulic head for inclined-throat curb inlets.
critic_review.governing_condition_default_exception: These are specific changes in v5.2.4; the release page alone does not establish that this is the latest release in every distribution.
critic_review.applicability: Supports version pinning and source tracking, not a diagnosis of the site.

critic_review_metadata.scope: Primary-source verification of consequential claims and limits in the investigator package.
critic_review_metadata.source_id_policy: Original S01-S12 IDs, titles, and URLs preserved; critic notes are appended per ID without rebinding.
